For the given triangular current waveform (sawtooth wave) from $t = 0$ to $t = T$, the equation of the current is given by:
$$\i(t) = \frac{I_m}{T}t$$

### 1. Average Value ($I_{\text{avg}}$)
The average value over one complete time period $T$ is:
$$I_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} i(t) \, dt = \frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} \frac{I_m}{T}t \, dt$$
$$I_{\text{avg}} = \frac{I_m}{T^2} \left[ \frac{t^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{T} = \frac{I_m}{T^2} \left( \frac{T^2}{2} \right) = \frac{I_m}{2} = 0.5 I_m$$

### 2. RMS Value ($I_{\text{rms}}$)
The root-mean-square value is given by:
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} i(t)^2 \, dt} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T} \int_{0}^{T} \left(\frac{I_m}{T}t\right)^2 \, dt}$$
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_m^2}{T^3} \int_{0}^{T} t^2 \, dt} = \sqrt{\frac{I_m^2}{T^3} \left[ \frac{t^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{T}}$$
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_m^2}{T^3} \left( \frac{T^3}{3} \right)} = \sqrt{\frac{I_m^2}{3}} = \frac{I_m}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 0.577 I_m$$
proTip: Always write the equation of the straight line for the given time interval before integrating for RMS and average values.
